text:
Iris: heads-up — we promoted ember-q1-int4 to canary and are seeing a spike in funcall structured-output parse failures (2.7% vs baseline 0.6%). copying a minimal raw from the assembler.
Noah: paste the snippet?
Iris:
```
INVOKE id=em-421 slice=17/48 model=ember-q1
OUT >> {\"tool\":\"ranker\",\"items\":[{\"id\":\"r1\",\"score\":0.98},
...<slice ends>...
---next slice---
INVOKE continue id=em-421 slice=18/48
OUT >> {\"id\":\"r2\",\"score\":0.95}],\"meta\":{}}
parser: JSONError: unexpected token '{' at position 1
```
Taj: looks like the slice boundary split the array/object and we ended up with two leading `{` tokens to the parser.
Noah: any correlation with request size / batch size?
Iris: yes — mostly at >1.4k token requests and when continuous-batching is active. smaller batches rarely fail. bench-bot: canary digest -> baseline 0.6% -> canary 2.7% (n=1800). breakdown: unexpected-token 46%, EOF 38%, other 16%. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/canary/1835004321
Taj: hypothesis: int4 quant shifts tokenization boundaries which moves punctuation/structural tokens across slice cutpoints more often. current batch-cutter is token-index based and blind to structural tokens.
Noah: mitigation ideas ranked quick->invasive: 
- assembler buffer-until-balanced-braces (bounded wait) ✅
- overlap-replay: prepend last N tokens of prev slice when merging ✅
- token-aware cutpoints: ask tokenizer for structural-token indices and avoid cutting on them (harder, might need tokenizer in runtime) ⚠️
- model-side sentinel suffix (e.g., `\\n__END_TOOL__`) — requires prompt changes ⚠️
- post-parse repair heuristics (append `]}` or try NDJSON reassembly) — diagnostic only ⚠️
Iris: I prefer trying buffer + overlap first since it's low-risk. we can add telemetry for `reassembly:buffered`, `reassembly:overlap_used`, and `preflight:midjson_detected`.
Taj: quick prototype: buffer until braces balanced OR wait 120ms max, then if still unbalanced attempt overlap merge with last 12 tokens. if still failing, mark `repair_applied` and run the simple repair heuristics in diagnostics mode only.
Noah: we should also add a tiny preflight lint on the first streaming chunk to cheaply detect likely mid-JSON scenarios (unbalanced braces, trailing comma, open string). tag those for special handling so we don't pay overhead for clean responses.
Iris: good. any thoughts about token-aware cutter? I know it's more invasive but might be the long-term fix — have the cutter consult a `tokenizer.structural_mask()` to avoid splitting on structural tokens like `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `,` that map to single tokens.
Taj: yeah, if quant causes tokenization shifts then only a tokenizer-aware approach will fully stabilize boundaries. runtime would need a small tokenizer binary or remote service; we can A/B it later.
Noah: also watch out for base64-like long strings — even if JSON stays valid, decoding can fail if cuts break 4-char groups. add `b64:buffer_hint` heuristic for long strings as stopgap.
Iris: plan: 
1) Taj lands assembler flags `buffer_until_balanced_ms=120` + `overlap_tokens=12` (off by default) and a diagnostics parse-repair path.
2) enable flags for the canary with continuous-batch size halved for micro-canary (48->24) for 30m.
3) collect 200 failure samples and run offline tokenizer-diff fp16 vs int4 to pick potential structural token shifts.
4) if buffer+overlap reduces failures >75% -> bake into batch-cutter and consider token-aware cutter prototype.
Noah: timeline?
Taj: I'll push the assembler flag PR today, wire basic telemetry and collector upload to s3://canary-dumps/ember-q1/ and aim to flip for canary tomorrow AM.
Iris: thanks — please paste raw failed fragments here as you collect them. we'll keep this thread as the single triage place. :thumbsup:
